newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Soybean prices set to drop sharply in 1998 - Safras.
newsitem.headline: Soybean prices set to drop sharply in 1998 - Safras.

text.p: Soybean prices are set to fall sharply in 1998 as a bumper U.S. harvest, combined with a record 1998/99 Brazil crop, replenish low world stocks, independent consultant Safras e Mercado said.

"If you add the large harvest predicted in the United States and the jump in planted area forecast in Brazil, stocks will be completely replenished and liquid, bringing a sharp downward tendency to prices," Safras said in a weekly bulletin.

With the U.S. forecast to produce upwards of 70 million tonnes this year and Brazil's next harvest seen at 29.33 million tonnes, it may even be optimistic to expect domestic prices to remain close to the historical average, Safras said.
On the upside, ending stocks should recover sharply to 530,000 tonnes in the 1998/99 harvest year (February-January) from a critically-low 297,000 in 1997/98.

"Production of 29.3 million tonnes would cancel the effect of low beginning stocks and would tend to maintain offer very high (up seven percent), allowing the drastic reduction in the necessity for imports," Safras said.
Exports were set to remain stable at 7.8 million tonnes in 1998/99 but were unlikely to rise due to sharp competition from the U.S. and Argentina, it added.
Due to this and a forecast drop in prices, crushing should pick up to 20.2 million tonnes from 18.5 million tonnes in 1997/98, but this was still well below Brazil's capacity.
